hypotheses.reasoning: audit-consumer crashes deterministically on message msg-750657 at committed offset 618947 with a RangeError (call stack overflow in expandReferences). After each restart (restarts 1-3, with growing backoff) the consumer resumes at the same committed offset 618947 and re-crashes on the same message, so it never advances past it. This is a crash loop on one malformed or recursive message jamming the audit.events queue, which explains the CrashLoopBackOff and the rising lag. Earlier batches processed normally (#1720, #1726). A GC warning (#595, 870ms) is minor and not causal. No upstream service shows related errors; the other services have zero error+ lines.

The only other anomaly is a GC pause of 870ms at 06:05:36 with heap at 56% after collection. This does not indicate memory exhaustion and does not explain a deterministic crash on a single message. A stack overflow is per-message recursion, not heap exhaustion. Ruled out as the primary cause.

verdict.recommendedAction: Quarantine or skip offset 618947 (msg-750657) on audit.events to unblock the consumer, restart audit-consumer, and let lag drain. Then fix the unbounded recursion in expandReferences (guard cyclic or deeply nested references) and find the producer that emitted the self-referencing payload.
